text:
Top-hat on an uneven background
Remove a sloping, vignetted background with a top-hat and count the spots one threshold finds, before and after. Unit: Grey-level morphology: top-hat and gradient.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Reconstruction in 1D
Grow a marker under a 1D signal one geodesic dilation at a time: reconstruction, h-maxima, h-minima and minima imposition. Unit: Reconstruction and h-extrema.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Reconstruction on images
Fill holes, clear the border, open by reconstruction, and find one regional maximum per nucleus with the h-maxima transform. Unit: Reconstruction and h-extrema.

title: Interactive demos
section: Connectivity pairs: the digital topology paradox
text:
Connectivity pairs: the digital topology paradox
Choose the connectivity of the objects and of the background separately, and see a closed diagonal curve stop separating its inside from the outside. A 3D tab does the same with 6/18/26 voxels. Unit: Connectivity and labelling.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Labelling step by step
Flood fill with a queue or a stack, two-pass labelling with its equivalence table, and run-based labelling on a small editable grid. Unit: Connectivity and labelling.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Union–find forests
Watch naive unions build a chain, and union by rank and path compression keep the trees flat. Unit: Connectivity and labelling.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Moments of a shape
Edit a shape on a pixel grid. See its centroid, second-moment matrix, eigenvectors, equivalent ellipse, Euler number, and three perimeter estimates against the exact value at every resolution. Unit: Region properties and moments.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Shape features
Convex hull and solidity, form factor, Feret diameters with rotating calipers, inscribed and enclosing circles, and Fourier outlines. Includes a units switch, anisotropic pixels and mask-error controls. Unit: Shape features.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Filter and count objects
A pipeline from threshold to count, with a measurement table and a scatter plot linked to the label image. Brush a rectangle to filter objects, and compare border rules, including the unbiased counting frame. Unit: Working with label images.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Flooding a profile
Raise the water level over a 1D landscape and watch basins fill and dams appear; fill shallow basins with h, flood the derivative, or place markers. Unit: Images as landscapes: watershed by flooding.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Priority-queue flooding step by step
Pop one pixel at a time from the queue and see the decision, the queue and the watershed line; compare 4 and 8 neighbours, FIFO and LIFO. Unit: The flooding algorithm on a grid.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Watershed of an image
Flood the gradient of a test image or a micrograph and fight oversegmentation with smoothing, h-minima and clicked markers; replay the flooding. Unit: Watershed segmentation of a real image.

title: Interactive demos
section: Splitting touching discs with the distance transform
text:
Splitting touching discs with the distance transform
Drag two discs together and see when the neck of the distance transform is deep enough to split them; ellipses, holes, metrics and a nuclei image. Unit: Splitting touching objects with the distance transform.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Intensity features of one cell
Six cells with the same mask and the same total signal. Change the background offset, gain, noise, saturation and mask error, and watch the mean, median, MAD, edge/mean ratio, mass displacement and radial rings respond. The population and plate tabs add per-well aggregation and robust z normalisation. Unit: Intensity inside an object.

title: Interactive demos
text:
The grey-level co-occurrence matrix
Count pairs of pixels at a chosen distance and angle, and compare contrast, homogeneity, ASM, entropy and correlation for two texture patches, including two with the same histogram. Unit: Texture: co-occurrence matrices.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Neighbours, parents and children
Count neighbours in a cell population under three definitions, compare nearest-neighbour distances with a random pattern (Clark–Evans), handle objects at the image border, and assign spots to nuclei or cells. Unit: Neighbours, parents and children.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Colocalisation of two channels
The 2D histogram of two channels, with Pearson’s r, the overlap coefficient, Manders’ M1/M2 and draggable thresholds. Costes’ threshold search, block randomisation, and presets for the classic pitfalls (background, missing thresholds, bleed-through, shift). Unit: Colocalisation of two channels.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Sliding and scoring
Slide one signal over another and watch SSD, cross-correlation and NCC being drawn, each fooled in its own way. Unit: Finding a shift by sliding and scoring.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Template matching
Drag a template over a micrograph and see its NCC map and best matches. Unit: Finding a shift by sliding and scoring.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Cross-correlation with the FFT
The FFT computes the correlation for every shift at once: compare it with brute force, see wrap-around and padding, and watch each frequency vote. Unit: Cross-correlation with the FFT.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Phase correlation
Register two crops of a micrograph by cross-correlation, phase correlation or NCC, under noise, uneven light and without a taper. Unit: Phase correlation.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Stitching a mosaic
Nine tiles at jittered stage positions: pairwise shifts, the four candidates, chaining versus global least squares, wrong pairs and blending. Unit: From a peak to a mosaic.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Sub-pixel peaks
Parabola, centroid and upsampled DFT on a peak whose true position is known exactly, with the error for every fraction of a pixel. Unit: From a peak to a mosaic.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Drift correction
Correct the drift of a time-lapse by registering to the first frame, the previous one or key frames, and the drift of a localisation-microscopy acquisition from time blocks. Unit: From a peak to a mosaic.

title: Interactive demos
section: The energy of a line profile
text:
The energy of a line profile
Segment a noisy 1D profile: thresholding against the labelling with the smallest energy, found exactly by dynamic programming. Unit: Segmentation as energy minimisation.

title: Interactive demos
section: Maximum flow, one augmenting path at a time
text:
Maximum flow, one augmenting path at a time
Step through Ford–Fulkerson on a small graph, see the residual graph, and the minimum cut at the end. Unit: Graphs, cuts and maximum flow.

title: Interactive demos
section: The graph of a small image
text:
The graph of a small image
Pixels as nodes, t-links and n-links with their capacities, and the minimum cut; make your own cut and compare. Unit: Graph-cut segmentation.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Interactive graph cut
Paint object and background seeds and see the segmentation update. Unit: Graph-cut segmentation.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Fiedler vectors and normalized cuts
Split points or a small image with the second eigenvector of the graph Laplacian. Unit: Spectral partitioning and normalized cuts.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Grow a decision tree
Add points of two or three classes, grow a tree split by split, read the split scan and the error against depth, or fit a step function to an edge profile. Unit: Decision trees.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Bootstrap and averaging
Draw bootstrap samples and count the points left out, and see why averaging correlated predictors stops at a floor. Unit: Bagging and random forests.

title: Interactive demos
text:
A forest in the plane
Many trees on bootstrap samples vote: probability map, single trees, out-of-bag and test error, and the effect of the features tried per split. Unit: Bagging and random forests.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Feature importance
Impurity and permutation importance of a forest on a table of cell measurements, with duplicated and correlated features. Unit: Forests on feature tables, and feature importance.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Paint and classify pixels
Paint a few strokes, and a forest on a multiscale feature stack labels every pixel; look at the uncertainty, correct, and evaluate on a held-out region. Unit: Pixel classification with a forest.

title: Interactive demos
section: Fit a line scan with a small neural network
text:
Fit a line scan with a small neural network
Train a 1 → H → 1 ReLU network live and watch the hinges move. Unit: Neural networks.

title: Interactive demos
section: Classify points with a small neural network
text:
Classify points with a small neural network
Change the hidden layers, units and activation and watch decision regions and per-unit thumbnails form as the network trains. By hand, drag a single neuron’s line; with the training controls, see overfitting on validation curves. Units: From a neuron to a network, Learning.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Backpropagation step by step
A two-neuron network drawn as a computational graph: forward values, backward gradients with each edge’s local derivative, one update, and a finite-difference check. Unit: Learning: loss, gradient descent and backpropagation.

title: Interactive demos
section: Gradient descent on a loss landscape
text:
Gradient descent on a loss landscape
Start paths on a two-parameter loss and compare learning rates, mini-batch noise, momentum and starts in different valleys. Unit: Learning: loss, gradient descent and backpropagation.

title: Interactive demos
text:
One convolutional layer
A bank of eight 3×3 kernels, hand-made or learned, with their feature maps after ReLU. Shift the input or pool the maps. Unit: Convolutional networks.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Receptive fields of stacked layers
Stack convolutions, pooling and dilated convolutions, then click a unit to see which input pixels it depends on. Unit: Convolutional networks.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Inside a trained convolutional network
Draw or rotate a digit and follow it through a small trained CNN: feature maps, class probabilities, each unit’s favourite patches, occlusion maps, and training with and without augmentation. Unit: Convolutional networks.

title: Interactive demos
text:
A U-Net segments nuclei
A tiny trained U-Net against Otsu’s threshold on synthetic nuclei. Shows errors, Dice and feature maps, and the effect of removing skip connections, using a Dice loss, and domain shift. Unit: Segmentation networks.

title: Interactive demos
section: Matching predicted objects to true objects
text:
Matching predicted objects to true objects
Predicted nuclei from an error generator (jitter, outline bias, merges, splits, misses, specks) or edited by hand, matched to the truth at an IoU threshold: IoU table, greedy vs optimal matching, F1 against τ next to the pixel Dice, the PR curve and AP, and a second annotator as the ceiling. Unit: Matching objects: IoU, F1 and average precision.

title: Interactive demos
section: Correlation is not agreement: the Bland–Altman plot
text:
Correlation is not agreement: the Bland–Altman plot
Automated against manual counts (or object areas) with bias, scatter and proportional bias: the scatter plot with r, the ratio, and the Bland–Altman plot with bias and limits of agreement. Unit: Boundaries, counts and the uncertain ground truth.

title: Interactive demos
section: Hausdorff distance and average surface distance
text:
Hausdorff distance and average surface distance
Drag a predicted outline, add a thin spike or a stray fragment, and compare IoU, Hausdorff, HD95 and the average surface distance; the radius slider keeps the pixel error and changes the object size. Unit: Boundaries, counts and the uncertain ground truth.

title: Interactive demos
section: Five ways to split: leakage in validation
text:
Five ways to split: leakage in validation
A k-nearest-neighbour pixel classifier on twelve images from four days, tested with random pixels, random blocks, blocks with a buffer, by image and by day; with random labels, random pixel splits still score 78 %. Unit: Honest validation: leakage, splits and domain shift.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Peeking at the test set
Pick the best of k equally good settings on a test set and see how much the reported score overstates a fresh re-test; a validation set removes the optimism. Unit: Honest validation: leakage, splits and domain shift.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Pseudoreplication: cells, experiments and pairs
A simulated two-condition experiment shown as a SuperPlot, analysed with cells as n, experiment means as n and paired means, with false-positive rates and power over 1000 repetitions. Unit: From measurements to claims.

title: Interactive demos
section: Many features on a plate: multiple testing and confounding
text:
Many features on a plate: multiple testing and confounding
Hundreds of features tested on a well plate with gradients and edge effects: p-value histogram, sorted p-values with the uncorrected, Bonferroni and Benjamini–Hochberg lines, and a layout confounded with the plate gradient. Unit: From measurements to claims.

title: Interactive demos
text:
PCA as a linear autoencoder
Turn a one-number linear autoencoder on two-pixel images; train a nonlinear one on a curve. Unit: From PCA to autoencoders.

title: Interactive demos
section: The VAE loss in one dimension
text:
The VAE loss in one dimension
Move the encoder’s cloud and see reconstruction, KL and their sum. Unit: The variational autoencoder.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Generating images with a VAE
Encode, decode, walk and sample in the 2D latent space of handwritten digits and of synthetic cell shapes. Unit: Generating and exploring images.

title: Interactive demos
section: Four instance maps on one image
text:
Four instance maps on one image
Simulated network outputs (boundary class, distance, star-convex polygons, flows) turned into objects, with error sliders and merges/splits counted. Unit: From masks to objects.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Boxes, IoU and non-maximum suppression
Drag boxes to see IoU, step through greedy NMS on touching cells, and compare anchors with centre heat maps. Unit: Finding objects as boxes.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Self-attention on patches
Click a patch to see its attention weights over the whole image next to a convolution’s fixed footprint, and the image after one attention layer. Unit: Attention, transformers and pretrained models.

title: Interactive demos
section: Frozen features and a linear probe
text:
Frozen features and a linear probe
Paint a few strokes and train a probe on raw patches, the filter stack or a small self-supervised encoder; click for similarity or a prompt mask. Unit: Attention, transformers and pretrained models.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Calibration and temperature
A reliability diagram of a simulated classifier: make it overconfident, fix it with a temperature, then shift the domain. Unit: Attention, transformers and pretrained models.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Diffusion in 2D
Watch point clouds melt into noise and come back by repeated denoising, with exact or learned scores, few or many steps, conditioning and guidance. Unit: Diffusion models and generated detail.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Which details are real?
Restore a blurred cell with an exact generative prior: the posterior mean is blurry and honest, the samples are sharp and invent nucleoli. Unit: Diffusion models and generated detail.

title: Interactive demos
section: Hit-or-miss and thinning on a grid
text:
Hit-or-miss and thinning on a grid
Fit three-state templates (1, 0, don’t care), thin a shape template by template, and check which pixels are simple. Unit: Hit-or-miss and thinning.

title: Interactive demos
section: Medial axis: maximal discs and the grassfire
text:
Medial axis: maximal discs and the grassfire
Drag a shape’s corners and see its distance transform, its medial axis by three methods, the grassfire front, and the shape rebuilt from the axis discs. Unit: Medial axis, distance transform and reconstruction.

title: Interactive demos
section: From skeleton to graph: pruning and length
text:
From skeleton to graph: pruning and length
Turn a skeleton into nodes and edges, prune the spurs, and compare three length estimators on lines at any angle. Unit: From skeleton to graph: pruning and length.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Measuring neurons and vessel networks
Run vesselness, threshold, skeleton and graph on a synthetic neuron or vessel tree and compare length, branch points, Sholl profile, radius and tortuosity with the known truth. Unit: Measuring neurons and vessel networks.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Moments of any order
The labelling day’s shape canvas with moments up to order 4: the triangle of moments, the marginals, skewness and kurtosis, a pixel as a point or a square. Unit: Moments as projections onto monomials.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Which moments survive a transformation?
A reference shape and a moved, scaled, rotated or mirrored copy: raw, central and normalised moments and Hu’s seven invariants side by side, with pose normalisation. Unit: Normalisation and moment invariants.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Complex moments as turning arrows
Rotate a shape and watch each complex moment turn (p − q) times as fast; mirror it and every arrow is reflected. Unit: Normalisation and moment invariants.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Monomials, Gram–Schmidt and Legendre polynomials
Why monomials are a poor basis: their Gram matrix and condition number, Gram–Schmidt step by step, and 1D fits that break down in finite precision. Unit: Better bases: Legendre moments and reconstruction.

title: Interactive demos
section: Rebuild an image from its moments
text:
Rebuild an image from its moments
An image reconstructed from its moments up to order N with monomials, Legendre and Zernike polynomials, against a Fourier low-pass with the same number of coefficients. Unit: Better bases: Legendre moments and reconstruction.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Zernike polynomials and rotation
The Zernike pyramid with radial profiles and optics names, and a rotated copy of an image whose |Z_nm| stay while the phases turn. Unit: Zernike moments on the unit disc.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Active contours (snakes)
A closed chain of beads pulled by elastic and rigid internal forces and by the edge map, with GVF and balloon forces and the snake matrix on demand; from the units Active contours and The snake as a linear system.

title: Interactive demos
text:
The modes of a snake
The internal forces as a circulant matrix: eigenvalues per wave around the curve, the factor per step of the explicit and semi-implicit updates, and the contour’s own modes dying out; from the unit The snake as a linear system.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Procrustes alignment
Align one landmark set onto another step by step (centre, scale, rotate) with the 2D closed form, with reflection and rigid options, and generalised Procrustes on a training set; from the unit Shape models.

title: Interactive demos
text:
A point distribution model
PCA of aligned landmark shapes (hands, nuclei, leaves): modes of variation with ±3√λ sliders, alignment and correspondence failures, and projecting a dragged shape onto the model; from the unit Shape models.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Active shape model search
Suggest points along the normals, fit the pose, project and clamp, coarse to fine, with noise, occlusion and a snake for comparison; from the unit Active shape models.

title: Interactive demos
section: Slicing a surface: curves as level sets
text:
Slicing a surface: curves as level sets
Cut the surface z = φ(x, y) at height c and watch contours split and merge; click for the normal and the curvature. Unit: Curves as level sets.

title: Interactive demos
section: Moving fronts: the level set equation
text:
Moving fronts: the level set equation
Move curves with constant speed and curvature flow, see merging, splitting, swallowtails, the CFL limit and reinitialisation. Unit: Moving a curve: the level set equation.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Geodesic active contours
A front that brakes at edges and is pulled into them: shrink-wrap several objects, leak through a weak edge, get stuck in a concavity. Unit: Edge-based segmentation: geodesic active contours.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Chan–Vese: segmentation by regions
Two means and a short boundary: robust to noise and blur, λ = 0 is thresholding, holes appear, bad starts get stuck. Unit: Region-based segmentation: Chan–Vese.

title: Interactive demos
section: The DP table, step by step
text:
The DP table, step by step
Fill the table of cheapest paths cell by cell, see the candidates and pointers, backtrack, and compare with the greedy path and the number of paths. Unit: The DP principle: minimal paths on a grid.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Boundaries in polar coordinates
Unwrap the image around a draggable centre and find the best closed boundary by DP, with smoothness, edge polarity and three ways to close the curve. Unit: Closed boundaries: DP in polar coordinates.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Dijkstra step by step
The same grid without a fixed order: the smallest tentative pixel becomes final, the queue is shown sorted, and one raster pass is shown failing on a detour. Unit: When there is no order: Dijkstra and live-wire.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Live-wire
Click a seed and the cheapest path to the pointer follows in real time; fix anchors, close the contour, and see where the wire short-cuts or jumps to a stronger edge. Unit: When there is no order: Dijkstra and live-wire.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Fast marching vs Dijkstra
Arrival times of a front by fast marching beside 4- and 8-neighbour Dijkstra: circles instead of diamonds, image-based costs, and minimal paths by gradient descent. Unit: From Dijkstra to fast marching.

title: Interactive demos
section: Every state of a tiny Ising lattice
text:
Every state of a tiny Ising lattice
Click spins on a 2×2 or 3×3 lattice and see the energy, the partition function and the probability of every energy level; in sample mode a Gibbs or Metropolis chain fills in the exact bars. Unit: Energy and probability: the Ising model.

title: Interactive demos
section: The 2D Ising lattice and its phase transition
text:
The 2D Ising lattice and its phase transition
A 256×256 lattice sampled live: domains below T_c, noise above, clusters of all sizes at T_c; cooling, quenching and a T-scan against Onsager’s exact curve. Unit: Sampling, temperature and the phase transition.

title: Interactive demos
section: Denoising a binary image with an Ising prior
text:
Denoising a binary image with an Ising prior
Compare ICM, simulated annealing, Gibbs sampling (MPM), mean field and the exact minimum cut on a noisy binary image, by energy and by wrong pixels. Unit: Bayesian denoising with an Ising prior.

title: Interactive demos
section: Quadratic, Huber and TV smoothing in 1D
text:
Quadratic, Huber and TV smoothing in 1D
Denoise a profile with a step, a ramp and a narrow peak under a quadratic, Huber or total-variation prior; see prior samples and the matrix I + λL with its frequency response. Unit: Quadratic smoothing and total variation.

title: Interactive demos
section: Points and their curves: the Hough duality
text:
Points and their curves: the Hough duality
Drag points in the image plane and watch their sinusoids in (θ, ρ) meet when the points are collinear; switch to slope–intercept form to see why it fails for steep lines. Unit: Hough transform: lines.

title: Interactive demos
section: Line detection with the Hough transform
text:
Line detection with the Hough transform
Edge points, the (θ, ρ) accumulator and the detected lines or segments, with controls for the bin size, the threshold, NMS, clutter and gradient voting. Unit: Hough transform: lines.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Circle detection: rings of votes
Each edge point votes for a ring of possible centres, or for one or two dots along its gradient. Scan the radius, change the polarity, and read a radius histogram at any centre. Unit: Hough transform: circles.

title: Interactive demos
section: The generalised Hough transform: R-table and voting
text:
The generalised Hough transform: R-table and voting
Build an R-table from a template you can edit, then find translated, rotated, scaled and occluded copies in a cluttered scene. Unit: The generalised Hough transform.

title: Interactive demos
text:
RANSAC step by step
Draw minimal samples, count the inliers within ±ε, refit, and compare with least squares and with the Hough transform of the same points, together with the probability of success after N samples. Unit: Hypothesise and verify: RANSAC.

title: Interactive demos
section: Running totals and the summed-area table
text:
Running totals and the summed-area table
Fill an integral image step by step and sum any rectangle from four signed table entries, or see a range sum as the rise of a running total. Unit: Integral images.

title: Interactive demos
section: Box filters: four methods, and repeated boxes
text:
Box filters: four methods, and repeated boxes
Count and time a k × k box blur done directly, separably, with running sums and with an integral image, and watch repeated boxes turn into a Gaussian. Unit: Box filters & local statistics.

title: Interactive demos
section: Local mean, standard deviation and precision
text:
Local mean, standard deviation and precision
Local statistics and contrast normalisation from the integral images of I and I², and what float32, wrapping integers and cancellation do to them. Unit: Box filters & local statistics.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Rectangle (Haar-like) features
Drag edge, line, diagonal and centre − surround templates over an image and see their table lookups, responses and response maps. Unit: Rectangle features.

title: Interactive demos
text:
A box feature stack
Box means, standard deviations, centre − surround and edge features at five scales; paint two classes and see which feature separates them. Unit: Rectangle features.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Boosting and the attentional cascade
Train a boosted detector stump by stump on cartoon faces or cells, build a cascade, and run it over a test scene. Unit: Boosted detectors & the cascade.

title: Interactive demos
text:
A linear classifier
Turn the normal vector w and shift the line; signed distances, nearest class mean, 1-NN and the perceptron. Unit: Linear classifiers.

title: Interactive demos
text:
The support vector machine in 2D
Add and drag points; the max-margin street, support vectors and slack, with C and (in other units) kernel functions and cross-validation. Unit: Maximum margin and support vectors.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Four loss functions
The 0–1, hinge, logistic and squared losses of a 1D classifier, each point’s loss and the average loss against the threshold. Unit: Maximum margin and support vectors.

title: Interactive demos
section: Lift and cut: the kernel trick as a picture
text:
Lift and cut: the kernel trick as a picture
Lift 2D points into 3D with a feature map; a plane there is a curve here. Unit: Kernel functions and the kernel trick.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Kernel functions in 2D
Linear, polynomial and RBF kernel functions, gamma and C, RBF bumps and the kernel matrix. Unit: Kernel functions and the kernel trick.

title: Interactive demos
section: An SVM in the pixel classifier
text:
An SVM in the pixel classifier
The random forests day’s pixel classifier with the SVM: standardisation, gamma, one-vs-rest vs one-vs-one, and cross-validation by stroke vs by pixel. Unit: SVMs for pixel classification.

title: Interactive demos
section: Training error, test error and cross-validation
text:
Training error, test error and cross-validation
A test set, error curves against C and gamma, and a 5-fold cross-validation map. Unit: SVMs for pixel classification.

title: Interactive demos
text:
k-means step by step
Assign points to the nearest centre, move centres to the means, and watch J fall; restarts show the local minima. Unit: Feature spaces & k-means.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Gaussians, ellipses and mixtures
Drag the axes of a 2D Gaussian, compare Euclidean and Mahalanobis distance, and mix two or three components with hidden labels. Unit: The multivariate Gaussian & mixtures.

title: Interactive demos
text:
EM step by step (1D)
E-step and M-step one at a time on a few points, with every responsibility and parameter in a table. Unit: Fitting a mixture: EM.

title: Interactive demos
text:
EM in 2D
Fit a Gaussian mixture to 2D points with any covariance type and start; watch the log-likelihood, restarts, collapse and BIC/AIC. Unit: Fitting a mixture: EM.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Grey-level mixtures
A K-class Gaussian mixture fitted to an image histogram: labels, probability maps, Bayes boundaries and multi-level Otsu. Unit: Mixtures on images.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Colour segmentation with mixtures
k-means against full-covariance mixtures in RGB, Lab and Lab + position, with Dice against the truth and low-likelihood anomalies. Unit: Mixtures on images.

title: Interactive demos
section: The Haar transform step by step
text:
The Haar transform step by step
Averages and differences of an 8- or 16-sample signal, one level at a time, with the reconstruction from the coefficients you keep. Unit: Localised basis functions and the Haar transform.

title: Interactive demos
section: Sparsity in two bases: Fourier and wavelets
text:
Sparsity in two bases: Fourier and wavelets
Keep the K largest coefficients of a 1D signal in the Fourier and in a wavelet basis and compare the errors. Unit: Localised basis functions and the Haar transform.

title: Interactive demos
text:
The wavelet filter bank
Low-pass and high-pass filters, keep every second sample, and back: perfect reconstruction, aliasing when a branch is missing, borders, the cascade and the basis functions. Unit: Multiresolution, filter banks and Daubechies wavelets.

title: Interactive demos
text:
The 2D wavelet transform
Subband pyramid of an image, reconstruction from the largest coefficients or without whole bands, and a comparison with Fourier and the 8×8 DCT. Unit: The 2D wavelet transform and sparsity of images.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Denoising by wavelet shrinkage
Hard and soft thresholding of the wavelet coefficients of a noisy image, the universal threshold, the noise estimate from the finest band, and cycle spinning. Unit: Denoising by wavelet shrinkage.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Build a Huffman code
Drag the bars of a histogram and build its Huffman tree merge by merge; compare the entropy, the average code length and a fixed-length code, and decode a message by walking the tree. Unit: Information, entropy and entropy codes.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Prediction and residuals
Predict each pixel from its decoded neighbours (left, up, average, planar, Paeth, MED) and see how narrow the residual histogram becomes, with entropies and real DEFLATE sizes; add noise to find the floor. Unit: Prediction, dictionaries and lossless formats.

title: Interactive demos
section: One block in three bases: DCT, DFT, KLT
text:
One block in three bases: DCT, DFT, KLT
Take one 8 × 8 block apart into DCT, DFT or KLT basis images, keep the largest or the first coefficients, and compare the energy compaction of the three bases. Unit: Transform coding, the DCT and the KLT.

title: Interactive demos
section: Periodic or mirrored? DFT against DCT
text:
Periodic or mirrored? DFT against DCT
Drag the 8 samples of a row and compare its periodic extension (DFT) and mirrored extension (DCT), their coefficients and the row rebuilt from the first k. Unit: Transform coding, the DCT and the KLT.

title: Interactive demos
text:
The JPEG pipeline
Compress an image with JPEG at any quality: follow one block through DCT, quantisation, zigzag and Huffman bits, see blocking, ringing and colour bleeding, and plot PSNR and SSIM against the file size. Unit: The JPEG pipeline, artefacts and quality metrics.

title: Interactive demos
text:
Same MSE, different quality
Five distortions tuned to exactly the same mean squared error: PSNR cannot tell them apart, SSIM can. Unit: The JPEG pipeline, artefacts and quality metrics.

title: Interactive demos
text:
What compression does to measurements
Store a synthetic 12-bit fluorescence image lossless, as JPEG or with a wavelet codec, and see what happens to spot counts, spot intensities, noise, texture and the 8-pixel blocking grid. Unit: Compression and measurements, JPEG 2000, formats.

title: Interactive demos

Projections and the sinogram
Turn the detector around an object, drop point masses and watch each one trace a sinusoid in the sinogram. Unit: Projections and the sinogram.

title: Interactive demos

Back-projection, angle by angle
Smear each projection back along its rays, with or without a ramp filter, and see the halo appear or cancel. Unit: Back-projection and the Fourier slice theorem.

The Fourier slice theorem
The 1D spectrum of a projection against the 2D spectrum along the same line, and direct Fourier reconstruction from spokes. Unit: Back-projection and the Fourier slice theorem.

How much data does a reconstruction need?
Angles, angular range, detector bins and dose for filtered back-projection; streaks, the missing wedge and noise. Unit: Filtered back-projection and sampling.

ART and SIRT by hand
A 2×2 or 3×3 image as a linear system with its null space, and ART zig-zagging between the measurement lines of two pixels. Unit: Reconstruction as a linear system.

Iterative reconstruction with priors
ART and SIRT with non-negativity and total variation against filtered back-projection: semi-convergence, few views, a missing wedge. Unit: Reconstruction as a linear system.

Spectra, filters and the mixing matrix
Drag dye peaks and filter bands and watch bleed-through, the mixing matrix and the condition number change. Unit: Bleed-through and compensation.

Unmix a lambda stack
Unmix a four-component cell recorded in 3–32 channels by least squares, and watch the residual, similar dyes and photon noise. Unit: Least-squares unmixing.

The cloud, the cone and the simplex
Rotate a cell’s pixels in channel space, normalise the cone into a triangle, drag the endmembers and compare LS, NNLS and fully constrained solutions. Unit: Endmembers: the geometry of mixtures.

Finding the spectra

Colour deconvolution of H&E

One marching-cubes cell

title: Denoising, artefacts, and what you may measure
text:
About this lecture
Two questions to end the day:

When there is nothing to un-blur, only noise: the classical denoisers, each judged by what it destroys.

Gaussian, median, bilateral, non-local means; Wiener with no blur.
The method noise check: what did the filter remove?

A restored image is an estimate: which measurements survive restoration (total intensity), which do not (peaks, sizes, separations, counts), and what to report.

Slides titled The math give the formulas and proofs; the ideas are complete without them.

Last unit of the deconvolution day. The median is introduced here as a denoiser (course map); the morphology day places it among the rank filters (min, median, max), and the thresholding day recalls it in one line. Noise models, PSNR and its peak: camera noise unit (day 3). All PSNR values here use peak 255 (8-bit grey levels). Statistics of measurements belong to the evaluation day (day 16).
crumbs: Denoising and what you may measure

title: Denoising, artefacts, and what you may measure
text:
Nothing to un-blur
With PSF = a single point (H = 1), Wiener and Tikhonov become denoisers: gain 1/(1 + 1/\mathrm{SNR}(f)), a low-pass filter chosen by the SNR per frequency.
Classical denoisers differ in what they average:









method
averages over
keeps
destroys




Gaussian
neighbours, by distance
nothing in particular
edges and noise alike


median
the middle value of the window
steps, against outliers
thin lines, corners


bilateral
neighbours that are close and similar
edges
ramps (cartoon), detail at the noise level


non-local means
pixels whose whole patch looks similar, anywhere nearby
repeated texture
unique fine detail
crumbs: Denoising and what you may measure

title: Denoising, artefacts, and what you may measure
text:
Gaussian and median
Gaussian: a weighted mean of the neighbours (the filtering unit). Linear: noise and edges are averaged alike, so every edge is blurred.
Median (a rank filter): sort the values in the window and take the middle one.
Row (10, 10, 10, 200, 10, 10, 50, 50, 50), window 3 (edges mirrored):



mean
